notes: would_upstream: no earlier decision carries would_upstream true (node hsdd/scripts/auto/state.mjs upstream prints none), so the request adopts, contradicts or leaves open none. This step adds one: DEC-013, RFC-001's version-1 statements (in-memory accounts and sessions, two endpoints, no database, no router) resolved locally; its authors should amend it or write an RFC for version 2.

cites-superseded is close to unconditional in this run: run.yaml's baseline sources carry version 1, and the condition matches any standalone 1 (1 to 64 characters, minLength 1, numbered list items). Every citation-touch the block lists will be dispatched, and so will any the insert rule adds. The block lists touches only for the four node specs, which cite the baseline paths (DEC-015).
supersededStrings also treats auth-api@v0 and profile-api@v0 as superseded (a v1 contract's lower version with no file counts as bumped in place). No file cites @v0, so nothing follows here.

PRD v2 Left to engineering: the longest booking and how far ahead go to H3, booking-api@v1's draft (DEC-011); whether signing in survives a restart goes to H1, ADR-001's update (DEC-008). RFC-001 section 6's no-router note goes to the web's D4 at H16 (DEC-012).
If H1 makes sessions survive a restart, simple-login.integration.2's AC-2.3 test loses its expired-token stand-in (a backend restart); H1's prompt names this and the record's prose routes it to H18.

H4 touches auth-api@v1 (stable, versioned) and H5 profile-api@v2 (stable, additive-only). If either classifies its change as breaking, H4 meets a breaking-amend stop; a new version that deprecates the old one triggers the insert rule's citation touches.
